```plato

    //==
    // # Quality readings
    //
    // Measurements that let a caller ARGUE that a pattern is blue rather than
    // assert it. Three independent readings, because each one is fooled by
    // something the others catch: spacing says nothing about anisotropy,
    // discrepancy rewards the lattice-like patterns that look worst, and the
    // spectrum is the only one that separates "even" from "regular".

    // The distance from point `index` to the nearest other point, or the largest
    // representable number when there is no other point. The per-point reading a
    // caller histograms: uniform random points give an exponential-looking
    // histogram with mass at zero, and a blue-noise set gives a narrow bump with
    // nothing below its radius.
    NearestNeighborDistance(index: Integer, points: Array<Point2D>): Number
        => points.Count.Range.Reduce(Number.MaxValue, (best, j) =>
            j == index ? best : best.Min(points[index].Distance(points[j])));
```
